llm.summary: This memory skill is not clearly malicious, but it broadly stores and reuses private conversation data and includes risky automation for prompt injection, remote LLM summarization, file restore, and generated skills.

dimensions.detail: The scripts default to a broad local memory tree, index profile/archive/daily content, may send memory excerpts to any configured LLM_API_URL, and include restore/generation paths that lack containment validation.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: No hidden installer was found; scheduled tasks, daemon usage, and hooks are described as user-configured or manually invoked. Users should still review cron/daemon setup carefully because it can run memory processing repeatedly.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill documents automatic session-start recall, session-end summarization, preference extraction, and direct prompt/system-prompt context injection without strong trust boundaries, preview, opt-in, or deletion controls.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The skill persistently writes daily logs, profile files, contact data, user graphs, FTS indexes, state files, generated skills, trigger databases, and symlinks; this persistence is disclosed but broad and under-scoped.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The core memory, search, archive, and recall features fit the stated secretary-memory purpose, but automatic skill generation and self-improvement expand into creating persistent agent behavior beyond ordinary memory management.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install only if you are comfortable with a persistent local memory system that profiles conversations and can recall that data into future prompts. Disable or avoid automatic skill generation, remote LLM summarization, daemon/watch modes, and restore operations unless you have reviewed the configuration and trust the memory directory contents. Prefer an isolated non-root memory directory and periodically inspect or delete stored profile, graph, index, and generated-skill files.
llm.findings:
[TP4] unexpected: I verified incomplete integration: ProfileMinerIntegration leaves its UserModel member unset, so graph updates can fail. This is a reliability and integrity concern, not evidence of malicious intent.
[SQP-2] expected: Automatic summarization, preference extraction, user graph construction, and cross-session recall are disclosed and purpose-related, but the artifacts do not provide clear opt-in, retention, inspection, or deletion boundaries.
[SDI-2] unexpected: The skill creator can generate new skill files and register triggers; this is a high-impact capability that crosses the boundary of a memory tool even though it is documented.
[SSD-3] expected: The profile and graph scripts mine preferences, habits, contacts, names, emails, entities, and relationships from session text; this is related to user modeling but creates a meaningful privacy concern.
[LP3] unexpected: The package has many scripts using file I/O, environment-controlled paths, optional network LLM calls, daemon monitoring, and generated artifacts, but metadata does not declare a tight permission or allowed-tool scope.
[SQP-1] unexpected: The trigger description covers broad memory, search, organization, and architecture terms, increasing the chance of activation when the user did not intend persistence or recall.
[T09] unexpected: The LLM summarizer sends memory excerpts, paths, dates, partitions, and query text to the configured LLM_API_URL without HTTPS, host allowlist, redaction, or per-request approval; the default localhost URL is rejected, so this is configuration-dependent rather than hidden exfiltration.
[T02] unexpected: Recalled memory is concatenated into prompt text and documented as suitable for system-prompt use without sanitizing instruction-like content, creating a plausible persistent prompt-injection path.
[T09] unexpected: Restore operations trust archive log and CLI path values when building source and destination paths, so a tampered restore log or crafted path can move files outside the memory tree within the process permissions.
[T09] unexpected: The skill generator sanitizes only the directory name, then reuses the unsanitized name in generated Markdown, Python source, and the Python filename; this can enable path traversal or generated-source injection if untrusted input reaches generation.
